_made_with.ns3: ns-3.42, 5G-LENA (nr) v3.3, build profile default (assertions on)

after_the_sweep.runs_made_again: the 100 runs with adaptiveRetx=1 (design study, repeat timer 'three round trips'): the timer was corrected (round trip taken from exchanges that needed no repeat, never longer than the fixed timer). They use the test-bed link.
after_the_sweep.all_other_runs: are the sweep's. The two sources differ only in that timer, which no other run uses.
after_the_sweep.ns3_tree: the earlier study's module contrib/pqc-security and its helper scripts were removed after the sweep (archived in docs/legacy) and the simulator was built again; the sweep's program was linked with that module and never called it
after_the_sweep.repeatability: Test-bed runs: byte-identical when made again with the rebuilt program (11 of 11 sampled). NR runs: one program started with the same arguments gives the same result every time (2 configurations run twice each, with and without address-space randomisation; 1 configuration with fresh memory filled with five different bytes: all identical), but the result changes in its last digits with what changes the layout of the program's memory: another build (the sweep's own source built in the cleaned tree does not give the sweep's bytes either), other allocator settings. The rebuilt program gives the sweep's bytes for 3 of 10 sampled NR runs. The cause is inside ns-3 / the NR library (the simulator itself keeps nothing ordered by address) and was not located. What that changes in the reported numbers: results/rebuild_check.json
